pencereler.0-5: The earthquake lasted a minute. The fire burned for three days. It destroyed eighty
pencereler.5-12: percent of San Francisco. So why could nobody put it out? The quake had shattered the water mains under
pencereler.12-20: the streets. Firefighters opened the hydrants and nothing came out. Broken gas lines and toppled stoves started hundreds of fires. Three thousand
pencereler.20-30: died and a quarter million lost their homes. It was the fire, not the quake, that did most of the killing.

segmentler.metin: San Francisco burned for three days.
It took only a magnitude 7.9 earthquake.
So how could a magnitude 7.9 earthquake do this?
The answer is fire following earthquake with broken water mains — and it is why cities now plan for fire after earthquakes, with independent emergency water supplies.
